trade.invalidation: The relative-value claim is false if official NZ yields (currently unavailable) show a large AU rate premium consistent with the 5y FX extreme; if subsequent AU housing/activity data stabilize or reverse while NZ labor/activity remain weaker (gauges 32/47/38 versus AU 50/54/48); or if AUDNZD makes a new high alongside a genuine AU-NZ inflation or policy re-widening rather than a USD residual.
trade.mispricing: AUDNZD at 1.2388 is 99.80 1y / 99.96 5y percentile (z_5y +2.96) after +2.94% 1m / +1.29% 3m, despite inflation gauges that do not justify an Oceania blow-out. The 1m decomposition is AUDUSD +0.54% versus NZDUSD -2.33%; the market has already treated NZ as the weaker economy, so additional AU housing deterioration and an NZ-specific trade catalyst are not in a still-rising 5y extreme. Carry of the fade is unknown because official NZ yields are unavailable; that gap cuts confidence, it does not authorize substituting a USD pair.

NZ labor 32 / consumer 38 / activity 47 are already weaker than AU 50/48/54, so the 5y extreme may be a fair NZ-growth discount rather than a mispricing.
AU inflation 82 can keep the RBA higher-for-longer even as housing breaks, supporting AUD on policy while NZ eases into weak labor.
Commodity terms-of-trade (iron ore versus dairy) and positioning are not in the packet.
ECB EUR-cross construction is not executable; live AUDNZD can differ from 1.2388.
Risk-off that hits NZD beta harder than AUD would extend the extreme.
trade.thesis: The intended differential is Oceania-relative, not a dollar view. Australia and New Zealand print almost identical inflation gauges (AU 82 vs NZ 80), yet ECB-implied AUDNZD sits at a 5y extreme after a +2.94% one-month grind. That richness is the residual of a still-firm AUDUSD (74.8 1y / 83.5 5y percentile) against a cheap NZDUSD (21.2 1y / 11.5 5y). Fresh AU evidence shows the RBA tightening channel now biting housing (NSW stamp-duty receipts -24% YoY, volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values down more than 7% from peak), while New Zealand just passed an India trade agreement cutting tariffs on about 95% of NZ exports. Short AUDUSD would contaminate the AU housing hit with a just-delivered, >90%-priced Fed 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%. Long NZDUSD would contaminate the FTA with the same USD residual. AUDCAD is the wrong alternative: it is also statistically rich (5y 99.56 percentile) but CA-AU 2Y is -167.5bp, so fading AUD there shorts a verified high-carry currency against cooler Canadian inflation (gauge 55, headline 3%, core near 2%). EURAUD looks cheap (1y 1.79 percentile) only because EURUSD is already 13.3 1y percentile after the Fed move; that is a USD-policy residual, not a clean EA-AU differential. AUDNZD isolates policy, growth, inflation, valuation and catalyst asymmetry without the dollar.
why_now: AU housing-tightening evidence printed 2026-09-16, the same day NZ's India FTA passed, against an AUDNZD 5y extreme dated 2026-09-17.
The Sep 16 FOMC 25bp hike is now a known USD event (>90% priced into the decision); leaving USD in the expression now owns residual dollar beta rather than the Oceania discrepancy.
AUDNZD 20d RV is only 4.83 and 60d RV 5.13, so the extreme is a grind, not a crash spike that has already mean-reverted.
